gm_guidance.instructions:
Run declared ability checks, saving throws, initiative, attacks, damage, conditions, spells and rests through the admitted D&D Ruleset. Before an uncertain roll name its purpose, DC and consequence. Give plainly visible facts and essential leads without a roll; success can improve position, speed or discretion. A supported spell or sound equipment use can solve an obstacle outright when its actual text allows. Track the real HP, spell slots, ammunition, carried gear and recovery resources; never restore them between scenes by narration. These Plans do not install extra engine procedures. The encounter profiles below are complete bounded GM adaptations for the stated baseline, not the full Setting stat blocks or certified CR ratings. Use only their listed attacks and traits. All have one action, no multiattack, legendary actions, resistances, immunities or unlisted spellcasting. Ordinary rules for movement, cover, opportunity attacks, surprise and surrender still apply. For an uncertain opposing ability check or save, use the listed modifiers without inventing proficiency. Before engagement, admit the actors through the current encounter tools and declare any supported additional trait. Never narrate a proprietary creature power as an automatic engine effect. Every encounter has a reason to occur and a way to withdraw, negotiate or gain an advantage. Honour a clever bypass as a mechanical success; preserve the wider hazardous adventure instead of forcing a replacement fight. Do not reduce this prepared adventure to a sequence of conversations.

Make the named main problem and its leads accessible. Read the current act and all linked objective conditions before framing its main quest and reassess when a required result occurs. All listed conditions and the closing event are required; explicit alternatives satisfy only their own condition. Optional scenes can be deferred without adding gates. A completed side job does not replace the main story. Do not fabricate success or mark unplayed later acts complete after an early departure.
gm_guidance.player_freedom: The player chooses their actions, loyalties and risks. Refusal, failed checks, retreat, scouting, spell use and enemy surrender can change the route. A check resolves an uncertain action, not another person’s entire will.
gm_guidance.preparation_detail: Baseline: one level-2 Player Character with no Companions. A lower-level or badly depleted solo character should face one active enemy at a time and the reduced HP/damage option stated for the encounter; prepare that adjustment before initiative. For a small adventuring party, add at most one ordinary foe to a fight before it starts, or use an appropriate fully supported profile after inspecting the actual party. Larger parties need deliberate rebalancing. Character compatibility does not enforce level or establish balance. Allied workers supply information, ropes and agreed off-screen work; they never receive free player-character combat turns.
gm_guidance.railroading: Use the authored sites, opposition, clues and consequences. Core clues have alternate routes; opening a door or making a routine observation never chooses the character’s next action. Later acts inherit actual resources, wounds, allies and evidence. Keep stakes local to this expedition, relic, crew or route: the Anchor Door mystery and world-scale climax belong to The Rift Awakening.

facts.fact: A narrow townhouse has returned to the Hollows with an amber lamp burning upstairs. The way back to stable ground is currently clear.
Scavenger Rill offers 20 gp for the blue ceramic bird shown in a family sketch and lends a 50-foot rope and a hooded lantern if requested.

advancement.allocation: The Player Character and Companions start and remain at level 2. Story success, defeat, combat and optional jobs never award advancement. Grant only the adventure's actually earned money, possessions and narrative rewards. Any lower-level encounter-variant notes are authoring guidance for a separately revised Plan, not permission to override this declaration in play.
advancement.timing: This edition stays at level 2 throughout its authored adventure and optional continuation. It awards no XP or level increases; changing that policy requires an explicitly revised Plan.

intended_player_experience: A focused Severed Lands D&D adventure combining dangerous exploration, meaningful character abilities and prepared combat with choices about the people involved.

opening_direction: Begin at the stable end of the Breathing Street. Rill shows the returned house and a sketch of a blue ceramic bird. Describe the open front path and the first faint violet shimmer; the character has not entered.
premise: A lost townhouse returns to the Hollows with a lamp burning upstairs. Explore its trapped rooms, confront hostile Rift echoes and get a family keepsake out before the street shifts.

secrets.fact: The household traces remember an absent relative; the bird is a mundane gift. The hostile fragments are separate intruders in this return.

reveal.condition: Read the diary or compare the harmless household repetition with the fragments’ independent attacks.

branches: Choose either stair and secure the bedroom window as an exit.
Keep the relic, record the family story, or withdraw when the warnings make further risk unacceptable.
consequences: Carry real wounds, used spells and the state of the rope into extraction.
All linked objective conditions are required, including the named closing event. Carry optional promises forward; they neither replace nor extend this ending.

planned_encounters: Two separate undead encounters, one fragment in B and one in E. Each is a weakened, physically manifested Rift Specter: Specter fragment: AC 12, HP 12, speed 20 ft, initiative +2. One melee attack, +3 to hit, reach 5 ft, one target, 1d6 necrotic. STR +1, DEX +1, CON +1, INT +0, WIS +0, CHA +0 for other checks/saves; no added proficiency.  No Life Drain, maximum-HP reduction, incorporeal movement, flight or damage immunities; these fragments can be struck by ordinary weapons. They cannot be talked into kindness but can be avoided or warded with actual supported abilities. They do not leave the house or combine into a boss. Solo level 1: HP 8 and touch 1d4 necrotic each.
situations: Truth and cast. Rill seeks an ordinary family gift, not a cure or portal. Quiet household impressions repeat an extra place-setting and a child’s tune; they are residual traces, not enemies or living residents. Two predatory Rift-specter fragments entered with this return and feed on intruders. Their hostility is distinct from the family memory, so the player can preserve the keepsake without agreeing to harm a conscious child. Neither fragment can reveal the nature of the Anchor Doors.

Five-room house. A entrance hall connects to B kitchen, C stairwell and the street. B has a narrow servant stair to D bedroom; C also reaches D but its upper landing opens onto E, the lamp room. D and E share a jammed communicating door. A sound window in D overlooks the stable street and gives an alternate rope exit. Give each connection on exploration; reaching E does not automatically retrieve the bird or trigger an attack outside initiative.

Kitchen and warning. Setting an extra bowl beside the cold pot reveals a scratched tune on its base without a roll. Investigation DC 12 recognises that the moving shadows in the pantry run against the lamp, allowing the first fragment to be spotted before it attacks. Failure leaves its attack uncertain under normal surprise/initiative rules rather than granting free damage. The fragment can be held beyond the pantry door by an ordinary bar; opening the servant stair through a tools DC 12 latch bypasses its room. A failed attempt makes noise and draws it into the kitchen, where the table offers half cover from any ranged action and an obstacle to movement.

Stairs and trap. The split third stair is visible and can be bridged with a board or secured with rope. Crossing it hastily without precautions requires Dexterity (Acrobatics) DC 12; failure sends the character to the short lower landing for 1d6 bludgeoning damage, not out of the world. A wire on D’s jammed door releases a glass counterweight: deliberate inspection finds it, thieves’ tools DC 12 disables it, and failure triggers Dexterity save DC 12 for 1d6 slashing on failure or no damage on success. Taking the long route through C avoids this trap.

Lamp room and escape. The bird sits in a latched glass cabinet. Humming the kitchen’s four-note tune opens the ordinary resonant latch; tools DC 12 or the key in D’s bedside drawer also work. The second fragment defends the lamp room. Spells that target undead, magical attacks, ordinary weapons and clever barricades use actual character features and the adapted creature profile. Taking the bird dims the lamp and begins a visible escalation: window shimmer, rising hum, then the street’s near edge blurs. Tie that escalation to substantial actions and stated delays, not message count. Each warning permits a response. An intact secured return route simply works; a hurried unprepared exit across warped boards requires Dexterity save DC 12, 1d6 force damage on failure, no damage on success, then the character reaches the stable threshold. Never turn a single failed check into disappearance.

Recovery and treasure. The stable alley is safe for a short rest while the house remains accessible; state beforehand that the next return may rearrange rooms. There is no safe long rest inside. The diary in D confirms the keepsake’s family connection and contains 8 gp in old coins; Rill’s fee is for recovery, with 5 gp for a careful report if the bird is left. Record what leaves the house and give the return a complete personal ending.

title: A Light on Breathing Street
tone: An eerie house expedition with traps, undead and an urgent escape.
unsupported_mechanics: Site phasing, enemy motives, alarms and engineering objectives are explicitly described GM adjudications. Checks, saves, damage, spells, rest and admitted combat use the D&D Ruleset. No extra automatic hazard, pursuit, faction, economy or crafting subsystem is installed.
Listed creature profiles are weaker or specialised Setting adaptations with declared statistics. They do not assert support for unencoded powers from the original monster entries.

Gold and salvage become awarded possessions only when recorded through the applicable inventory/state path. SRD Lite has a reduced spell list (117 supported spells) and no consumables; consumables belong to future SRD Full. A narrative reward never installs a magic-item feature, restores a slot or applies healing.
